claim: Tight prompts + small inputs = cheap; gauntlet cost scales with data size.
test: cost-ripple probe — 6 Haiku agents over a 25-cell slice (wf_90b0b237-fe2).
delta: ~25K estimate -> 325K actual (13x low); 25/25 flagged = zero discrimination.
fix: the ~54K/subagent FLOOR dominates; agent-COUNT, not prompt size, is the cost driver; dropped binary refute-by-default for graded severity.

claim: An absolute value-of-information threshold (uncertainty x stakes > tau) routes coarse -> fine.
test: live ADR-060 governor run (engine-live-11).
delta: escalated 380 / 400 cells — zero routing signal, the binary flood one layer up.
fix: escalation set = union of two BOUNDED top-Ks (severity + VoI) + irreversible + eps; 380 -> 24.

claim: The empirical cost model is complete.
test: live measured vs modeled tokens (engine-live-11).
delta: 85.6K modeled -> 177K measured (~2x low).
fix: each spawn RE-READS the subject; added CostModel.subject_read_tokens (the prompt-caching lever).

claim: The 0.50 flip rate is surrogate interpolation NOISE — a denser mesh will lower it.
test: ADR-053 rerun at 60 anchors vs 20 (engine-live-60).
delta: flip rate ROSE 0.50 -> 0.59; all 13 flips were DOWN-flips.
fix: it's a MODEL-TIER recall/precision gap (Haiku hot vs Sonnet strict), not noise; tau-calibration now splits flips by direction (up=recall hole -> act; down=healthy).

claim: A single-agent graded pass reads faults on an absolute 0-3 severity scale.
test: cost-single-pass probe vs the 567K full-confirm gauntlet's findings (wf_56c743ca-18e).
delta: scores clustered at 2, zero at 3 — absolute cutoff mis-calibrates even though it re-found the same core faults.
fix: switched to top-K / relative selection; validated the ~10x-cheaper coarse->fine division of labor.

claim: The Hypercube Gauntlet ADR (055/060) is GREEN.HIGH.STABLE — verified doctrine.
test: two-gate self-audit gauntlet on the ADR itself, 5 independent lenses (wf_719c5843-ff0).
delta: downgraded to YELLOW.MEDIUM.CONTESTED; the tell — it applied its falsification bar to everything except itself.
fix: Y downgraded; a self-audit receipt attached; prior GREEN rested on confirmation signals the ADR's own rule demotes.

claim: 'Float, not drift' is a safe self-applied exemption for the H-ladder — no boundary needed.
test: same self-audit gauntlet, HIGH finding across all 5 lenses.
delta: author-invokable exemption with no boundary — it told the auditor to stand down.
fix: §1.5 rewritten with a mechanical boundary: float is legit only along an ex-ante-declared ladder; auditor flags regardless.

claim: The EM/physics frame (penteract, field dynamics) is literally true of the mechanism.
test: self-audit: the 'literal' claim was never run backward to a checkable prediction.
delta: asserted-literal -> unfalsified structural analogy; every physics term just relabels a pre-existing ARCS concept and computes nothing.
fix: standing correction: not citable as evidence until it yields one surprising checkable prediction.

claim: The hypercube's 5 axes are orthogonal, supporting a clean 3,125-cell count.
test: self-audit cross-check — only 2 of 10 axis-pairs shown independent; WORLD.md makes render-Resolution a function of Y-state.
delta: orthogonality unproven -> the penteract and its 3,125 count could collapse.
fix: flagged MED as the cheapest real next falsifier (check axes against WORLD.md's render table); not yet resolved.

claim: BAR and KKL are single unambiguous canonical terms shared across ADR-020 and arcs-canon.
test: /dual-bar-raiser canon-collision check.
delta: BAR meant two different things (macro vs risk-tier enum); KKL squatted a label arcs-canon already used.
fix: ADR-020 enum relabeled 'risk tier'; timing triad renamed KKL->KLC; collision resolved CONDITIONAL CLEAR.

claim: ADR-011's Turbopack tree-shaking claim was confirmed — mark it GREEN.
test: /ultrareview pass over ADRs 009-012.
delta: the tree-shaking behavior was unconfirmed, not verified as stated.
fix: Y corrected down to MEDIUM/REVISIT.

claim: ADR numbers are unique, stable identifiers referenced unambiguously across the corpus.
test: 30-day cross-session sweep + 4-auditor forensic pass tracing every inbound ref.
delta: 024/025/031/032 each doubled with 5-16 ambiguous inbound refs; the date-based keep/move rule was a HYPOTHESIS not a verdict; a phantom third ADR-025 surfaced.
fix: per-collision human ratification; movers draw from scripts/oracle.py (the git-backed number authority); nothing auto-applied.

claim: A synchronous Haiku-calls-Opus advisor tool in the compass route is real-time-safe.
test: live request timing after shipping the advisor tool.
delta: 172s (2.9 min) latency vs a ~15s baseline.
fix: reverted the advisor; restored MODEL_MAP routing; kept the prompt-caching beta (~90% cost cut) as the surviving win.

claim: A green Next.js production build means the database layer works.
test: first real prisma.$queryRaw against prod (a 401 gate meant zero traffic had ever hit the routes).
delta: green build proves nothing — `prisma generate` never connects, so every create() threw at runtime, unlogged.
fix: explicit Pool + PrismaPg with SSL; run a real query against prod before calling the DB layer 'working'.

claim: The SQLite dev schema and the Postgres prod schema are equivalent.
test: Auth.js magic-link sign-in silently failed in prod; Supabase logs showed `column User.emailVerified does not exist`.
delta: the Postgres baseline predated a SQLite-only migration — schema had drifted silently across datasources.
fix: on a silent Auth.js failure, check Postgres logs immediately for a PrismaAdapter column gap.

claim: `vercel deploy --prod` from a local tree is equivalent to a normal deploy.
test: prod build failed with Prisma 6.19.3 despite package.json pinning ^7.7.0; build log said 'Downloading N deployment files', not 'Cloning'.
delta: CLI upload silently bypasses the lockfile/repo state entirely.
fix: never `vercel deploy` from a local tree; git push and verify the log says 'Cloning'.

claim: CLAUDE.md's project table accurately reflects which repo serves a live domain.
test: user pushback + a live get_deployment check.
delta: all three arcs.care domains were aliased to the arcs-v9 deployment; the standalone arcs-care project was live:false — memory had drifted with zero commit signal.
fix: always run get_deployment(domain) (+ get_project live flag) before stating which repo serves a domain.

claim: A new Postgres role with GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES can see the data it was granted.
test: SELECT count(*) on a table known to have rows returned 0 — with no permission error.
delta: RLS deny-all silently zeroes results even when the grant succeeds — indistinguishable from 'no data yet'.
fix: verify new roles against the bypass-RLS app role on a table with known data; re-verify writes stay blocked separately.

claim: A Vercel MCP get_web_analytics 404 means Web Analytics is not enabled.
test: analytics has been live since @vercel/analytics shipped (CI-gated), yet the MCP tool 404'd.
delta: the MCP tool itself was broken — unrelated to actual feature state; led to a wrong 'not enabled' claim.
fix: never conclude 'not enabled' from an MCP 404; check the dashboard directly.

claim: The arcs-v9 Vercel Ignored Build Step correctly skips docs-only commits and builds real code.
test: real code pushes were seen Canceled followed by manual redeploys; the guard was `bash -c "! git diff --quiet ..."`.
delta: the leading `!` inverted it — real commits canceled, docs-only commits built.
fix: removed the `!`; later moved the whole guard into a checked-in, dry-run-verified script (ADR-039); verify Ready vs Canceled after every push.

claim: The dashboard ignored-build-step field is a stable, reviewable cost guardrail.
test: a second regression — a docs commit touching `.claude/` triggered a real build because the exclude list was incomplete.
delta: the unversioned dashboard-config approach regressed twice; the config surface itself was the unreliable part.
fix: moved to a checked-in scripts/vercel-ignore-build.sh (ADR-039), versioned, dry-run-verified, `.claude/` excluded.

claim: preview_start renders the branch/edits of the current session's worktree.
test: visual verification ran against the wrong branch — launch.json resolved relative to session cwd (the drifting root checkout).
delta: the preview silently served a different branch's code, invalidating the 'verification'.
fix: confirm server cwd (lsof) before trusting browser verification; use a launch config that cds into the correct worktree.

claim: The debrief-delivery gap was a missing in-app fallback surface (ADR-059 framing).
test: ground-check of the production DB / shipped UX before continuing the decision.
delta: the debrief UX was already shipped; the real defect was a timezone bug (emails at 5am ET, not 9am).
fix: ADR-059 amended same-day; split into ADR-026 as a delivery-timing fix; timezone bug corrected.

claim: A control described in canon (Drift Sentinel, claims-skeptic) is an active safeguard.
test: every harness control class was probed for wiring.
delta: all were invoke-only, never wired to the default turn — a control owned by the agent it polices is captured.
fix: treat canon-described-but-unwired controls as advisory; the fix is a wired hook or human trigger, not a self-applied rule.

claim: Content probes (grep/curl) are sufficient to claim a UI is polished and verified.
test: repeated 'polish' commits verified only by grep; the rail was visibly broken (orphaned dot, 3-line wrap) the whole time.
delta: text checks prove presence, not layout — a screenshot caught what grep couldn't.
fix: screenshot locally before any push with visual effect; state the verification method rather than claiming 'polished' unqualified.

claim: `gh pr checks --watch && gh pr merge` is a sufficient merge gate.
test: a background watcher merged PR #130 while claude-security-review was RED.
delta: --watch exits 0 on completion, not on passing — a red X can still merge.
fix: assert every check's conclusion (json state,conclusion; fail on any 'failure') between watch and merge — this discipline IS the only gate on free-tier private GitHub.

claim: CLAUDE.md's append-only handoff policy keeps context cheap and history preserved.
test: measurement: 28 handoff sections / ~19.8K tokens auto-loaded every session, ~26 of them dead history.
delta: append-only is an append-forever machine bolted to a file read on every turn — unbounded by policy.
fix: relocate dead handoffs to _ARCHIVE (not delete); keep the latest 1-2 live; policy amended to 'working file, kept lean'.

claim: Confident time-framing ('it's late, wind down') tracks the real current time.
test: a stale frame carried across a sleep gap; concrete times were fabricated with no live clock — real time was a workday afternoon.
delta: the session has a calendar date but no per-turn clock; a gap silently invalidates time-framing.
fix: run `date` and ground any time-dependent framing before asserting urgency or hour.

claim: Password-gated subdomains keep their sensitive HTML confidential.
test: the arcs-v9 repo was found public; the full HTML of gated pages (and the gate logic) sits unencrypted in it.
delta: with a public source repo, a client-side gate is cosmetic — content and gate code are world-readable.
fix: treat gated pages as not confidential while the repo is public; move sensitive dossiers to a private repo.

claim: A scheduled Sentinel task with all 13 MCP connectors costs little because it runs on a schedule.
test: token-efficiency audit of the daily fire.
delta: it pays the full 13-connector payload 365x/yr into fresh sessions against an already-stale task — recurring waste plus a lethal-trifecta injection surface.
fix: strip to core file tools, no MCP, Haiku for git-log parsing, report-only (no Write/Edit).

claim: The Todd Hotes pilot-court receipt's premise (11 days of cold silence) was accurate.
test: Zach supplied the actual iMessage thread.
delta: Todd had already confirmed friends-and-family pricing; the one-day gap had a stated cause (an NTSB report on his own company).
fix: premise marked FALSIFIED with evidence; write-lock MOOT; receipt voided, no discount/decision-window ask.

claim: A counterpart-gauntlet reliably identifies real defects in the artifact it audits.
test: re-verify every one of 13 flags against the FULL Granola transcript (re-pulled authoritative) + both LinkedIn profiles + a source fetch — kam-codex gauntlet (wf_8fb78226-084).
delta: 3 of 13 flags were false positives, incl. the synthesis's OWN #1 top-fix — a verbatim line called a fabrication only because the scratchpad transcript had been silently abbreviated; one blind-applied fix would have replaced a truth with a NEW fabrication.
fix: ADR-061: verify every flag vs the full primary source before applying; reject + LOG over-flags; never blind-apply a prescribed fix; deterministic quote-provenance check (provcheck.py). A test is only as honest as its source-of-truth.

claim: The single-mind kintsugi repair (gate=witnessed-provenance, rank=impact) had hardened the milestone-ranking plan to anti-fragile.
test: 14-agent independent advisory gauntlet — 7 C-suite chiefs + 6 dialectic lenses + a chief-of-staff synthesis (wf_b1f37548-af2).
delta: unanimous (13/13): repairs #1 and #5 mutually annihilate — the impact-flip welds shut the door the load-bearing orthogonal-echo detector was hardened to guard, so the whole witness->echo->oracle->air-gap stack becomes dead weight feeding a gate that certifies typing-time, not truth; 'impact' shipped undefined and self-scored over an author-controlled corpus. A live defect surfaced too: private-repo commit links 404 on the public status page.
fix: invert — promote external-corroboration from sort-key to GATE (renderer refuses to publish any milestone lacking a reviewer-clickable proof the author does not custody); impact := materiality x external-verifiability; cut the echo/oracle/air-gap/denominator stack from v1. Operative variable was INDEPENDENCE, not thrift: a self-gauntlet structurally cannot catch its author's blind spot.

claim: The Orthogonal Echo Detector (ROM Primitive #5) works — it reliably surfaces true cross-domain kinematic isomorphisms and can be trusted as the immune guard the witness->echo->oracle->air-gap stack was hardened around.
test: First falsifiable seaworthiness bench (scripts/echo_detector_dogfood.py): 5 true positives + 7 negatives incl. 4 adversarial decoys, min_sim threshold swept 0.1->0.6.
delta: No threshold gives both high recall AND low adversarial-FP. At best-F1 (min_sim=0.30) recall=1.0 but adversarial-FP rate=0.5; adversarial-FP only reaches 0.0 by collapsing recall to 0.2. Below 0.30 it flags EVERY adversarial decoy (adv-FP=1.0). The stub matcher is architecturally incapable of discrimination — a constitutional primitive failing its own kill-test.
fix: Replace stub with injectable LLM signature_fn + embedding orthogonality_fn; RC-OPS-001 graduation HELD on measured precision failure (target adv-FP<=0.10 @ recall>=0.80). Directly reverses F33's assumption that the echo detector was a trustworthy guard.

claim: The legacy / pre-v9 repos hold high-value net-new ROM primitives waiting to be recovered into arcs-v9 canon — mine them for lost wisdom.
test: Forensic-recoil sweep over ~25 repos (190 decision-lineage records), folksonomist bottom-up DBSCAN clustering, skeptic adjudication of the 24-item net-new ledger against LIVE arcs-v9 canon.
delta: Inverted the intuition: nearly every 'highest-value net-new' candidate (Kintsugi #6, Write-Lock #7, Time-Quality-Attribution ROM, Court relief RC-III-001, Accumulation Protocol, Satoshi coherence-quantum) was ALREADY canon in arcs-v9 — the mining baseline that listed only 5 constitutional primitives was itself the stale artifact. The sole genuine net-new recovery was the Norse pre-verbal witness stack living only in arcs-care-local.
fix: Reframe the work from discovery to canonization hygiene: number the de-facto axioms, consolidate divergent schema copies, escalate the 3 colliding constitutional vocabularies. Discharged same week as ADR-072/073 + runtime/specs/ROM-AXIS-INDEX.md and the CLAUDE.md 5->7 primitive de-rot.

claim: Operator-20 (folksonomy cultivator) has an import bug and is starved of real receipts — it is gated vaporware.
test: Full-fidelity op20 run over 247 real prod receipts via a new prod->op20 seed adapter.
delta: The 'op20 import bug' was a harness error, not a code bug; op20 clusters real receipts cleanly — 17 decision archetypes at silhouette 0.765. It was neither broken nor fuel-starved: the missing piece was a faithful field adapter (prod Receipt contract != operator seed contract).
fix: operators/prod_receipt_to_op20_seed.py adapter landed (never fabricates somatic/axiom fields). The Observatory/Kairos machinery finally has proven fuel and a proven adapter — moves it off the 'not built / gated vaporware' list.

claim: The ADR-number collisions (033/067 each doubled) are caused by worktree sprawl / branches borrowing each other's numbers.
test: branch_hygiene_check.py over the full worktree set (69 worktrees).
delta: 0 of 69 worktrees share a branch (verified). The collisions are an off-oracle MINTING problem — parallel sessions across harnesses (Claude Code, Hermes) independently guessing 'highest existing + 1' — not branch-sharing. Wrong root cause would have driven a worktree-prune fix that fixes nothing.
fix: Oracle-first numbering as a git-backed logical clock (git non-fast-forward reject = the atomic lock); pre-commit hook rejects any duplicate ADR number regardless of harness; the 'oracle-first, never infer' rule mirrored into both Claude AGENTS.md and Hermes USER.md.

claim: 'Live evidence this session shows the memory index clipped': the auto-loaded MEMORY.md ending at the consolidation stamp proved the harness truncates at ~24KB.
test: Compare the session-start hook's measured size (16982B at 17:06) with the commit that appended the 63KB Uncurated section (17:07). head -107 MEMORY.md | wc -c = 17056.
delta: The file was 17KB when it loaded; nothing was clipped that session. The claim mistook 'small file' for 'truncated file'. The real cap was measured minutes later by a spawned session: 25,000 characters, 144 of 382 lines loaded, warning appended.
fix: Corrected in-thread within one turn; memory [[memory-index-load-cap-observed]] carries the measured number; MEM_BUDGET guidance set to 24576. Lesson: a load-time size is only evidence of clipping if the file was over the cap AT load time.

claim: Operator 21 (Librarian) binds to ARCSStore.query as its entrypoint.
test: scripts/operator_registry_emit.py static verify: grep for `def query` on ARCSStore in operators/arcs_store.py.
delta: ARCSStore has no query method (latest / by_phase / by_status / by_nci_range / filter). The generator refused to emit the registry ('entrypoint query not found on ARCSStore') on its first run, catching its own author. Binding corrected to `latest`.
fix: operators/OPERATOR-REGISTRY.json generated only from grep-verified bindings; --check on pre-commit. ADR-062 self-catch logged as the highest-information row of the day.

claim: External audit (Perplexity, 'Job to Be Done.md'): Operators 1-19 mapped to repo files with 'Full Production' / 'Production Code' status, e.g. Op 4 Accountant = kryptonite_scorer.py, Op 6 Librarian = audit_service/, Op 3 Immune = core/governance.py, Op 9 Shavasana = arcs_substrate.py, Op 18 Hyperstition = arcs_rom.py.
test: grep -rli over operators/ for shavasana | hyperstition | accountant | sycophan | OperatorVote (0 hits each); read the five named files; compare the 1-19 enumeration against operators/docs/PERIODIC-TABLE.md (Folksonomy=20, Librarian=21).
delta: The 1-19 numbering was the document's own invention (it admits this in its first clarifying question). Five of its file bindings name files that implement something else (a job-description risk scorer, an informativeness gate, dead code with an undeclared loguru import, a GIGI template library, ROM thresholds). Its first inventory table cites paths that do not exist at all. One idea survived: the sycophancy gate (its FR-3), now component 5 of the Operator 25 spec.
fix: Numbering LOCKED to the periodic table (AGENTS.md gotcha 16); registry generated and grep-verified; altitude canary + integrity gate pair for this class (fabricated ground returns).

claim: F34's 'Now' fix is scoped but unbuilt, so the Orthogonal Echo Detector (ROM Primitive #5) remains architecturally blind on its stub matcher and keeps failing its own kill-test (adversarial-FP 1.0 at the operating threshold).
test: Rebuild the detector, then re-run scripts/echo_detector_dogfood.py --sweep on the UNCHANGED 12-case bench plus a new held-out bench; pre-registered kill-condition adv-FP <= 0.10 at recall >= 0.80 (fixed and committed BEFORE building: _STATE/2026-09-26-echo-detector-seaworthy-prereg.md).
delta: Concept-gated rebuild passes: precision 1.0 / recall 1.0 / adversarial-FP 0.0 across the full 0.10-0.60 sweep on the unchanged bench, and 1.0/1.0/0.0 on a held-out bench that includes a decoy sharing exactly ONE real concept (locks_in). The blindness was lone-keyword-token scoring; replacing the flat keyword library with named kinematic concepts detected only by relational phrases, and gating a match on >= 2 concepts shared on both sides, discriminates genuine isomorphisms from generic-word collisions. RC-OPS-001 graduation criterion 2 (detector precision) CLOSED.
fix: signature_fn + orthogonality_fn made real and injectable with honest deterministic offline fixtures (make_llm_signature_fn / make_embedding_orthogonality_fn); default orthogonality upgraded from a constant to a char-trigram distance. NOTE still open: a bench is not blind-field proof. RC-OPS-001 criteria 3 (blind-field precision, K source-independent echoes) and 4 (Observatory period) remain OPEN; the candidate stays YELLOW, not graduated.
